title: Universal openness of module surjectivity with proper target support
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and use algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] and their sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Use quasi-coherent modules on small etale ringed sites and tensor pullback [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it is the cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules. Relative flatness means flatness of stalks on etale scheme charts over the local rings of the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. A finite type module is etale locally finitely generated; support proper over the base means there are a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z$ proper over the base and a finite type quasi-coherent module $N$ on $Z$ with $i_*N\simeq M$, as in [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Let $f:X\to B$ be locally of finite presentation [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], and let $u:F\to G$ be a homomorphism of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Assume $G$ is of finite type and has support proper over $B$. For each scheme $T\to B$ put $X_T=X\times_BT$ and let $u_T:F_T\to G_T$ be tensor pullback of $u$ along $X_T\to X$. Define the subfunctor $V_u$ of $B$ by $V_u(T)=\{b:T\to B\mid u_T:F_T\to G_T\text{ is surjective}\}$. There is an open subspace $V\hookrightarrow B$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] with natural identifications $\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,V)=V_u(T)$ for every $S$-scheme $T$. In particular factorization through $V$ characterizes surjectivity after arbitrary, including nonflat, base change. No finite type assumption on $F$ or flatness assumption on $G$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $C=\operatorname{Coker}(u)$. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits] it is quasi-coherent. The images of any finite local generating family of $G$ generate its quotient $C$, so $C$ is of finite type. Tensor pullback is left adjoint to the specified direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]; hence [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], applied to the finite cokernel diagram, gives $\operatorname{Coker}(u_T)\simeq C_T$ for every $T\to B$. In particular $u_T$ is surjective exactly when $C_T=0$. No left exactness of tensor pullback is used.

By [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-support-pullback], $D=\operatorname{Supp}_X(C)$ is closed. Since $C$ is a quotient of $G$, a zero stalk of $G$ gives a zero stalk of $C$, so $D\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}_X(G)$. Choose the proper closed carrier $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $i_*N\simeq G$ from the hypothesis. Outside $|i|(|Z|)$ the direct-image chart diagram has only empty-source sections and its limit is zero [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]; therefore $D\subseteq|i|(|Z|)$. The point map $|i|$ is continuous [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], so $|i|^{-1}(D)$ is closed. Properness means universal closedness in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Thus $E=|f|(D)=|fi|(|i|^{-1}(D))$ is closed in $|B|$.

source.place: Tag 09TP, final sentence, using the proper-carrier meaning of support proper over the base.

proof.text: Let $O=|B|\setminus E$. The invariant-open quotient construction [lem-a1-space-invariant-open-quotient], applied to any etale scheme atlas of $B$, gives an open subspace $j:V\hookrightarrow B$ with point image $O$.

source.place: Tag 09TP, displayed open subset and reference to Tag 03BZ.

proof.text: Fix any $b:T\to B$ and write $p:X_T\to X$, $f_T:X_T\to T$. By [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-support-pullback], $\operatorname{Supp}(C_T)=|p|^{-1}(D)$. The stalk-conservativity theorem [lem-sfb-space-geometric-points-conservative], applied to $C_T\to0$, says $C_T=0$ exactly when this set is empty. Realize $D$ as the point image of a reduced closed subspace $H\hookrightarrow X$ using [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. Its base change $H_T\hookrightarrow X_T$ has point image $|p|^{-1}(D)$. Associativity of the sheaf fibre products identifies $H_T$ with $H\times_BT$. The arbitrary Cartesian point-image identity of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives $|f_T|(\operatorname{Supp}(C_T))=|b|^{-1}(|f|(D))=|b|^{-1}(E)$. A set is empty if and only if its image under a function is empty. Consequently $C_T=0$ if and only if $\operatorname{im}|b|\subseteq O$. This applies equally to nonflat base change.

source.place: Tag 09TP, support pullback and representability inference; Tag 03H4 point lifting made explicit.

proof.text: By [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests], $\operatorname{im}|b|\subseteq O$ is equivalent to unique factorization of $b$ through $j:V\hookrightarrow B$. Together with steps 1 and 4 this gives the required bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,V)\simeq V_u(T)$. For $T\prime\to T$, composition of the unique factorization gives the unique factorization over $T\prime$; tensor-pullback composition sends $u_T$ to $u_{T\prime}$. Hence the bijections are natural. The zero target yields $V=B$, and empty bases and empty fibres are included by the same empty-support criterion.

source.place: Tag 09TP, conclusion, with naturality of the representing bijection written out.
